question: Raja Reddy is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Reddy** is an Indian** Kuchipudi dancing couples,** gurus, and choreographers.
 
• He is renowned as exponents of the** south Indian dance form of Kuchipudi.**
 
• Their names are synonymous with Kuchipudi dance and are regarded solely responsible for bringing it on the cultural map of the world.
 
• For their services to the** field of arts**, the Government of India has conferred on them the** Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi:**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is a major classical dance form of India that originated in a village of the Krishna district of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• Kuchipudi involves different foot movements and is generally a team performance.
 
• The central them of Kuchipudi is Bhagavata puran.
 
• The dancers of Kuchipudi came to be known as Bhagavathalus.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is the oldest and major classical dance form of India that originated in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It traces its origins back to the Natyashastra, ancient treaties on theatre written by the mythic priest Bharata.
 
 
 
• **Odissi:**
 
 
• It originates from the state of **Odisha**, in eastern India.
 
• It is traditionally a dance-drama genre of performance art, where the artist(s) and musicians play out a story, a spiritual message, or devotional poem from the Hindu texts, using symbolic costumes, body movement, abhinaya, and mudra set out in ancient Sanskrit literature.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art and is the folk dance form of **Kerala**.
 
• It is a 'story play' genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colorful make-up, costumes, and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.
